Q: Why should I learn Javascript if I could just learn jQuery? A:

Today jQuery is not necessary. Plain JavaScript is beautiful to work with. Modern browsers/engines implement new ECMAScript standars pretty quickly. Understanding plain JS is a cornerstone that will, at a later point, prove you as an indespensable skill to understand other tools, frameworks, libraries, toolchains, built on top of it. Any you need zero dependencies to start with.

Q: Techinques/tools for embedded Linux boot optimization? A:

The basic rule is: the fastest code is code that never gets loaded and run, so remove everything you don't need:

  • in U-Boot: don't load and run the full U-Boot at all; use FALCON mode and have the SPL load the Linux kernel and DTB directly
  • in Linux: remove all drivers and other stuff you don't really need; load all drivers that are not essential for your core application as modules - and load them after your application was started. If you take this serious, you may even want to start only one CPU core initially (and start the remaining ones after your application is running).
  • in user space: minimize the size of the root file system. Throw out anything you don't need; configure tools (like busybox) to contain only the really needed functionality; use efficient code (for example, link against musl libc instead of glibc) etc.

What can be acchieved by combining all these measures can be seen in this video - and yes, the complete code for this optimization is available here.

Q: How to direct calculate the range of a float in C? A:

Also, floats are sign/magnitude so the finite values farthest from zero (biggest magnitude) are +-FLT_MAX. Unlike two's complement integers where they have different magnitudes. And yeah, they're not one away from powers-of-two, they're like 0xffffff << (max_exponent-23) for float with 24-bit mantissa (including the implied bit).

You can experimentally find the largest exponent with doubling while new_x > old_x. (INFINITY > INFINITY is false, so new_x and old_x are both infinity, and the last finite value was 2 iters ago.) Or while(new_x < INFINITY), then old_x is your finite value.

Then keep adding half, one quarter, one eighth etc. of that biggest finite power-of-2, as long as the additions don't make the value infinite. (while isfinite(x) or while (x<INFINITY), and repeatedly multiplying by 0.5f.) This will set lower bits in the mantissa until it's all-ones, with the exponent still being the max finite, all but one bit set.

BTW, INFINITY == INFINITY is true in IEEE FP math, so new_x == old_x would be another way to detect that you produced infinity. Or that an addition was lost to rounding error, if it rounded down back to one of the inputs.

Q: How to uninstall influxdb with all its data and configuration files A:

It depends on how you installed it.

If you installed it via the package manager on RHEL based distro, use:

yum remove influxdb

or

dnf remove influxdb

(Credit: larsks in the comment)

If you installed it using the binary, you should delete the content of engine-path and bolt-path.

Q: Spring boot suite start an old version A:

This is likely due to a mismatch between the Java and Spring Boot versions, not STS.

  • Check JDK: old Spring Boot needs Java 8/11

  • Don’t create new → import as existing Maven project

  • Run:

    mvn clean install

  • Then Maven → Update Project in STS

If it builds via Maven but not in STS, then it is an IDE issue. If Maven fails, fix pom.xml / dependencies.
